project with no editor window and a preview with no item to play, changing
nothing, and a preview still seeking after 5 s, which it has paused. It ends
paused where the play reached. It is
`playback_prefetch_proof.py`'s instrument.
**`graphic_memory {pressure?}`** (issue #127, §11 G-37) answers the graphic
rasters' one memory budget and the frames a document keeps. It needs no
project and runs off the main thread. `pressure` — `"normal"`, `"warning"` or
`"critical"`, any other value refused in its own sentence before anything
moves — first sets a SIMULATED memory-pressure level, which holds against the
system's real events until the tool sets `"normal"`; that clears the
simulation and applies the last real level. It answers `physical_bytes`
(`ProcessInfo.physicalMemory`), `budget_bytes` (a quarter of it at normal, an
eighth at warning, 0 at critical), `pressure` (the level in force),
`held_bytes` (every session's rasters held ahead now), `held_peak_bytes` and
`held_peak_entries` (the highest totals since the last answer, which resets
them to the current ones), `kept_bytes` and `kept_frames` (the kept frames'
total and count, over every document), `kept_hits` (how many compositor
requests the kept frames have answered since launch), `ahead_bytes` (the kept
frames a background pass drew ahead that the compositor has not passed, §11
G-38), `ahead_evicted` (those a trim pushed out while still ahead, since the
last answer, which resets it to 0), `pass_activity` (whether a running
background pass holds the App Nap opt-out), `image_cache_bytes` (what the
engine's decoded-image cache of PNG and JPEG assets holds, §11 G-39) and
`image_cache_limit` (its limit: `budget_bytes / 16`, 0 under
`FrameJobGraphicImageCacheOff`). It is `graphic_memory_proof.py`'s,
`background_render_proof.py`'s and `image_cache_proof.py`'s instrument.

**The transport is spec §11 MC-1..MC-6** (road map 14,
`designs/adr/roadmap-14-agent-socket.md`): the server listens only on a Unix socket,
`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock`, at every launch
(MC-1), bound by the first instance and only in its own `0700` `Agent`
subfolder the person owns (MC-2); an external client reaches it through
`framejob-mcp`, the bundle's stdio server (MC-3), which answers `initialize`
and `tools/list` without launching Frame Job and launches it in the background
on the first `tools/call` that finds no socket (MC-4); a tool call never
raises a modal question (MC-5); and `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` overrides the path,
which every proof sets (MC-6). The socket is bound at every launch
(`AgentServer+Socket.swift`) and is the only listener: road map 14's MC4
deleted the TCP one, its switch and MC-6's interim rule. A tool call decides
"may ask" where it hands work to the importer, so a person's own import
still asks while a call runs (MC-5). Settings' MCP section's Copy MCP
Command (MC-7) puts the `claude mcp add` line for the bundle's own
`framejob-mcp` on the clipboard; it is not an edit, so it has no tool.
- `AgentServer+DevTools.swift` — the dev tools' seam (road map 11, spec
  §11 V-1/V-2): the handler table, catalog rows and off-main set compiled
  only under `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`, which Debug and Release set and
  Distribution does not. The frozen file merges them (`withDevHandlers`, a
  union) and `catalogJSON()` splices the rows in BEFORE the file tools. It
  holds `devToolsMarker`, the string `tools/proof/dist_check.py` requires in
  Release's binary and absent from Distribution's, and absent from each
  bundle's assistant helper (D12, D13); a tool NAME cannot be the
  marker, because an `-O` binary stores a literal of 15 bytes or fewer
  inline. Its tables hold
  `snapshot_ui` (V2a), `perform_menu_item` and `cancel_sheet` (V2b),
  `select_inspector_tab` (V3), `assistant_send` and `assistant_answer`
  (road map 12 A1), `play_preview` (#127, G-36) and `graphic_memory` (G-37); a dev tool is counted apart from the product tools (`tools/proof/dev_tools.py`).
- `AgentServer+PlayPreview.swift` — `play_preview` (dev only, wholly under
  the flag; spec §11 G-36, §7.9c): plays a window's preview forward through
  the transport's own `setRate` and `seek(to:)` (an optional `seek_to` half
  way) on the SERVER thread, and answers the frames expected against those
  composed per key, compose milliseconds and, when asked, each frame's
  digest. `stale_ticks` (with `seek_to`, #329) reports those ticks to
  `GraphicPrefetch.reach` as requests reached after the seek, in the seek's
  own step or, with `stale_armed`, once a frame in the seek's first
  `armFrames` frames was composed (waited for at most `min(2 s, seconds /
  2)`); `stale_reached` answers the ticks reported. Its four refusals are
  read before the first hop to main. `tools/proof/playback_prefetch_proof.py`
  drives it.
- `AgentServer+GraphicMemory.swift` — `graphic_memory {pressure?}` (dev
  only, wholly under the flag, off main; spec §11 G-37): the graphic
  rasters' budget, held and kept bytes and their peaks, a pass's
  `ahead_bytes`, `ahead_evicted` and `pass_activity` (G-38), and
  `image_cache_bytes` and `image_cache_limit` (G-39), from
  `GraphicPrefetch.memoryReport`; `pressure` simulates a memory-pressure
  level until the tool sets `normal`. `tools/proof/graphic_memory_proof.py`
  drives it.
- `PlaybackTrial.swift` — `PlaybackTrials`, `play_preview`'s record (dev
  only): `Compositor.serve` reports each finished frame's time, compose
  time and, while a trial asks, a SHA-256 of the destination's pixels;
  `recorded(_:)` copies a running trial's record without ending it.
- `AgentServer+MenuItem.swift` — `perform_menu_item` and `cancel_sheet`
  (road map 11's V2b, dev only, wholly under the flag). It runs a main-menu
  item by path in a NAMED project window's own responder chain, never
  nil-targeted, and works with the app inactive and the window occluded
Before trusting any run, `grep "Frame Job: " <folder>/framejob.log` must print
nothing: that prefix is the startup check that the tool catalog matches the
core's op table. On a Debug build the same mismatch traps instead.

The instance still shares its bundle's settings domain, so never perform a
menu item that persists a setting (the View menu's Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide
Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview Quality) from a script.

A Debug or Release build, never Distribution, also has dev-only tools over
MCP: `snapshot_ui` (a capture of the editor, a sheet, Settings, Welcome or the
recorder panel, with a layout dump), `perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`,
`select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview` (plays a preview and answers the frames
composed), `graphic_memory` (the graphic rasters' memory budget, and a
simulated memory-pressure event) and `assistant_send` / `assistant_answer` (an
assistant turn against a stand-in server). To look at the chrome without a
running app or a Screen Recording grant, use the offscreen harness in
`tools/proof/harness/`.

The root [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) ("Verifying a build", "Verification",
"Seeing the chrome") has the full rules: what a proof may claim, which build a
recorded run drives, and the dev-only launch defaults.
[`tools/proof/README.md`](../tools/proof/README.md) lists the proofs, says how
to make their test media, and describes the MCP client and the harness. What no
script can confirm is a row in [`docs/manual-checks.md`](manual-checks.md),
which the owner runs before each release.
yellow bound is B < 100 because the built-in Display P3 screen gives the
fixture's sRGB yellow as [255, 255, 84].

python3 tools/proof/v2_snapshot.py <dir>/agent.sock [--log PATH] [--only T,N,O,C,F,A,L,P]

four of road map 11, then road map 12 A1's `assistant_send` and
`assistant_answer`, then #127's `play_preview` and `graphic_memory`) and reads the startup marker's count
(`dev_marker_count`). The scripts that assert an exact tool set subtract

`image_cache_limit` (its limit: `budget_bytes / 16`, 0 under
`FrameJobGraphicImageCacheOff`). It is `graphic_memory_proof.py`'s,
`background_render_proof.py`'s and `image_cache_proof.py`'s instrument.

**The transport is spec §11 MC-1..MC-6** (road map 14,
`designs/adr/roadmap-14-agent-socket.md`): the server listens only on a Unix socket,
`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock`, at every launch
(MC-1), bound by the first instance and only in its own `0700` `Agent`
subfolder the person owns (MC-2); an external client reaches it through
`framejob-mcp`, the bundle's stdio server (MC-3), which answers `initialize`
and `tools/list` without launching Frame Job and launches it in the background
on the first `tools/call` that finds no socket (MC-4); a tool call never
raises a modal question (MC-5); and `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` overrides the path,
which every proof sets (MC-6). The socket is bound at every launch
(`AgentServer+Socket.swift`) and is the only listener: road map 14's MC4
deleted the TCP one, its switch and MC-6's interim rule. A tool call decides
"may ask" where it hands work to the importer, so a person's own import
still asks while a call runs (MC-5). Settings' MCP section's Copy MCP
Command (MC-7) puts the `claude mcp add` line for the bundle's own
`framejob-mcp` on the clipboard; it is not an edit, so it has no tool.
- `AgentServer+DevTools.swift` — the dev tools' seam (road map 11, spec
  §11 V-1/V-2): the handler table, catalog rows and off-main set compiled
  only under `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`, which Debug and Release set and
  Distribution does not. The frozen file merges them (`withDevHandlers`, a
  union) and `catalogJSON()` splices the rows in BEFORE the file tools. It
  holds `devToolsMarker`, the string `tools/proof/dist_check.py` requires in
  Release's binary and absent from Distribution's, and absent from each
  bundle's assistant helper (D12, D13); a tool NAME cannot be the
  marker, because an `-O` binary stores a literal of 15 bytes or fewer
  inline. Its tables hold
  `snapshot_ui` (V2a), `perform_menu_item` and `cancel_sheet` (V2b),
  `select_inspector_tab` (V3), `assistant_send` and `assistant_answer`
  (road map 12 A1), `play_preview` (#127, G-36) and `graphic_memory` (G-37); a dev tool is counted apart from the product tools (`tools/proof/dev_tools.py`).
- `AgentServer+PlayPreview.swift` — `play_preview` (dev only, wholly under
  the flag; spec §11 G-36, §7.9c): plays a window's preview forward through
  the transport's own `setRate` and `seek(to:)` (an optional `seek_to` half
  way) on the SERVER thread, and answers the frames expected against those
  composed per key, compose milliseconds and, when asked, each frame's
  digest. `stale_ticks` (with `seek_to`, #329) reports those ticks to
  `GraphicPrefetch.reach` as requests reached after the seek, in the seek's
  own step or, with `stale_armed`, once a frame in the seek's first
  `armFrames` frames was composed (waited for at most `min(2 s, seconds /
  2)`); `stale_reached` answers the ticks reported. Its four refusals are
  read before the first hop to main. `tools/proof/playback_prefetch_proof.py`
  drives it.
- `AgentServer+GraphicMemory.swift` — `graphic_memory {pressure?}` (dev
  only, wholly under the flag, off main; spec §11 G-37): the graphic
  rasters' budget, held and kept bytes and their peaks, a pass's
  `ahead_bytes`, `ahead_evicted` and `pass_activity` (G-38), and
  `image_cache_bytes` and `image_cache_limit` (G-39), from
  `GraphicPrefetch.memoryReport`; `pressure` simulates a memory-pressure
  level until the tool sets `normal`. `tools/proof/graphic_memory_proof.py`
  drives it.
- `PlaybackTrial.swift` — `PlaybackTrials`, `play_preview`'s record (dev
  only): `Compositor.serve` reports each finished frame's time, compose

  `recorded(_:)` copies a running trial's record without ending it.

nothing: that prefix is the startup check that the tool catalog matches the
core's op table. On a Debug build the same mismatch traps instead.

menu item that persists a setting (the View menu's Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide
Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview Quality) from a script.

MCP: `snapshot_ui` (a capture of the editor, a sheet, Settings, Welcome or the
recorder panel, with a layout dump), `perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`,

composed), `graphic_memory` (the graphic rasters' memory budget, and a
simulated memory-pressure event) and `assistant_send` / `assistant_answer` (an
assistant turn against a stand-in server). To look at the chrome without a
running app or a Screen Recording grant, use the offscreen harness in
`tools/proof/harness/`.

to make their test media, and describes the MCP client and the harness. What no
script can confirm is a row in [`docs/manual-checks.md`](manual-checks.md),
which the owner runs before each release.

## Codec export C6a — the Export Queue's memory limit and the sheet's estimate (`encoder_limit_proof.py` B0, P0, R1–R3, E1–E3, Q1–Q5, S1, S2, X1, Z1; twelve mutants; `encoder_memory_measure.py`; spec §11 CX-18)

A queued `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` or `vp9_alpha_webm` job starts only while every bundled-encoder export
running in the app (the queue's and every Export… sheet's) fits, with it, in a quarter of
physical memory, each costed by its resident peak measured at 1080p and 4K; a held job says
why in its row and in `export_status`'s `waiting`. The sheet shows "Estimated time: about …"
on those rows.

```
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/encoder_memory_measure.py   # the per-key measurement
python3 tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py --probe                   # B0–Q5, no app
python3 tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py [--app debug|release|PATH] # adds S1, S2, X1, Z1
python3 tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py --mutant NAME             # exit 1 caught, 0 survived, 2 control
```

**`encoder_memory_measure.py`** launches one fresh instance per key and size (av1 and
av1_webm at faster, balanced and smaller; vp9_webm in an SDR and an HLG project;
vp9_alpha_webm, added in C5's fix pass; h264 as the AVFoundation control; 1920 × 1080 and 3840 × 2160), places AV.mov twice (10 s, 300 frames),
warms with one `render_frame`, reads the baseline `ps -o rss=`, then follows `export` to
`done` while sampling the RSS every 0.1 s: delta = peak − baseline, seconds = the done
answer's `elapsed`, the 1-minute load average at the start. It writes
`work/encoder-memory/<date>/memory.json` and prints the table `ExportEncoderCosts.swift`'s two
tables are transcribed from; the road map's "## C6a" records the run. A run that fails is a
row with its error and the script exits 1; a baseline RSS that cannot be read fails its row
rather than counting the whole peak as the delta.

**`encoder_limit_proof.py`**'s probe rows run `encoder_limit_probe.swift`, built through
`swift_build.build()` over `app/Sources` with `Blank.mp4`, `Fonts` and a `default.metallib` of
`Compositor.metal` and `ExportI010.metal` beside it in `work/encoder-limit/probe/`. **It needs
no instance:** its two live projects are built in the probe from AV.mov as
`webm_readers_probe.swift` builds A1's — A1 (640 × 360, AV.mov under a two-second text clip)
and W9 (1920 × 1080, AV.mov 24 times at scale 3) — rather than saved over MCP. The probe's
answer is raw; every expected value is computed in the script from P0's dump of the tables.
P0 the nine keys, each figure sourced; R1 the budget (physical / 4) and the identical jobs
admitted per key at 1080p and 4K = max(1, ⌊budget / cost⌋) on 16–128 GiB; R2 an unmeasured
writer row (a synthetic `unmeasured_webm`, every real row being measured) costs the whole
budget and runs alone; R3 h264 books nothing;
E1 the estimate per key at five sizes and three lengths; E2 `estimateText`'s steps; E3 none
for h264, nor for `av1` at a rate that cannot be stepped (no frame count). Q1 the live shared queue and ledger with physical = 4 × the sheet job's cost: a
headless Export… sheet writes W9 as `av1` Smaller while A (`av1`), B and C (`h264`) are
enqueued — A held with the exact sentence, B then C passing it and finishing before the
sheet, A launched only at the sheet's finish (each event stamped with a sequence number;
the sheet's finish is read at every queue and ledger notification, so a launch inside the
sheet's `end` reads after it); Q2 `export_status` for held A; Q3 at 1 TiB A runs beside a
sheet; Q4 the row's status line for held A and waiting C, and the

sheet's ledger `end`) never finish, its video pump blocked in `copyNextSampleBuffer`
(`designs/codec-export.md`, "Export hang (C5's fix pass)"). This runs the same sequence many
times, under load or idle, and counts the runs that stall.

```
python3 tools/proof/export_hang_soak.py --mode probe --runs N [--load K] [--stall-s S] [--variant NAME]
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/export_hang_soak.py --mode app --runs N [--load K] [--stall-s S]
```

**`--mode probe`** runs `encoder_limit_probe.swift` whole per run, built through
`encoder_limit_proof.build_probe` into `work/export-hang/build/<variant>/`, with four opt-in
environment knobs the probe reads (none set, its answer is unchanged): `RC_PROBE_TRACE`
(a JSON line a second and per `Watch.tick`: `{t, row, seq, sheet, jobs, ledger,
compositor}`), `RC_PROBE_HOLD_POOL=<n>` (n `Task.detached` bodies blocked for Q1's length),
`RC_PROBE_A_PRESET=<id>` (A's preset, default `av1`) and `RC_PROBE_SPIN_MIN=<s>` (every
`spin` timeout at least s; the runner sets `--stall-s` + 60). **`--mode app`** drives one
owned instance per 10 runs (relaunched after a stall) through the dev tool `export_sheet`
(spec §7.9c): `begin` W9 `av1` Smaller with `physical_memory` 4 × its cost (from the probe's
P0 tables), A (`av1`), B and C (`h264`) of A1 through `export`, then two `av1` jobs back to
back; a run is `error: unbooked` when the sheet's cost never reaches the ledger in 30 s and
`error: missed` unless A answered `queued` with `waiting` before the sheet finished.

**A stall** is `--stall-s` (120) seconds with no job's state or progress and no sheet's
progress changing. The runner samples the process twice (`sample <pid> 10`, 30 s apart),
records the last compositor counts (`asked`, `begun`, `done`, `answered`, `cancel_all`,
`CompositorRequestCounts`) and the stalled job (the running job or sheet that stopped first,
its row and when), classifies the second sample (token counts, the main thread's top five
frames, the thread count) and kills only its own pid. `--load K` starts K `/usr/bin/yes`
children and kills them at exit. Variants (probe only): `defer-launch`, `slot-before-read`,
`flush-after` (source copies, each anchor found once) and `hold-pool-12`, `a-preset-h264`
(knobs). `error` runs do not count toward `--runs`. Each soak writes
`work/export-hang/<date>/<mode>-<variant>-load<K>-<time>/summary.json` after every run.
EOF

### Fix pass 1 (2026-10-28): the held sentence in the tooltip, the review's nits, two residues

**The should-fix: the held sentence was unreadable.** The queue row's status label is one
mono line that truncates its tail, so at the window's width the held sentence lost its GB
figures, and the tooltip did not carry them either. `ExportQueueRowView.toolTip(for:)` now
ends with `job.message` while the job waits, so the whole sentence is a hover away. The row
stays one line: its height is fixed (52 pt) and a wrapped status label in its stack would
need its own width solving, so wrapping was not taken. The guide's export page says what the
window shows: one line, cut with "…" where it does not fit, and the whole sentence in the
tooltip; spec §7.8 says the same.

**The nits, all fixed (the owner's residue rule).**
1. `ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds` answers nil when `sequenceFrameCount` is nil (a rate
   that cannot be stepped), so the sheet shows no estimate line and `export_status` has no
   `estimated_seconds`, where before it estimated 0 frames as "about 5 s" and 0. CX-18 (9)
   and §7.8 say so.
2. `encoder_memory_measure.py` fails a case whose baseline RSS cannot be read, instead of
   recording the whole peak as its delta.
3. `docs/manual-checks.md` SE-20: the sheet's estimate line on each AV1 and VP9 choice, and
   a held queue row and its tooltip, in both appearances.

**The proof.** Q4 also reads `toolTip(for:)`: A's ends with the whole sentence, and C's has
no "Waiting for memory" line. E3 also takes `av1` at fps 0/1 (no frame count): no line, no
seconds. Two mutants were added, one per new branch: `tip-drops-hold` (Q4) and
`estimate-no-count` (E3).

**Residue 1: `phase7_chrome.py`'s four Document-pane failures, fixed in the instrument.**
Section 5 solves the translucent note's shift over a band written down in points. The
summary's Colour row (HD-2) and the Canvas section's Dynamic Range and Blending rows (HD-2,
HD-16) moved the Appearance section down about 95 pt, so the band (y 615) lay across the
Background swatch, which a background change redraws. The opaque control's winning shift
then left 35 rows unexplained. The note row was found at the Appearance header's Reset (y
584) instead of under it, and read white ink. Every check that read the band failed, on
main as on C6a. The constants were re-measured from the script's own renders: `ABOVE_Y1`
500 → 595, which cuts through the Reset (584–606 pt), so the Reset is recognised and
excused; `BELOW_Y0` 615 → 660, the rows under the Background row (Timecode, Fit, Markers).
Markers alone is now too short to clear `SHIFT_MARGIN` in the opaque control: a band at 724
gave a runner-up of 23 rows against the 40 required. At 660 the translucent render's
runner-up is 100 rows and the control's 74. No app file changed for this.

**Residue 2: `graphic/tests/path.rs`'s timing budget, made robust.** R2, R4 and R5 ran their
render under the 250 ms preview budget as the engine's wall-clock call deadline. A load
average near 100 stretched R4's wall time past it, and the engine interrupted the call ("over
the 250 ms budget at frame 7"). That is a flaky gate, not a slow path. `timed` now runs the
call under a 10 s deadline (`HANG_MS`, which only a hang trips) and asserts the calling
thread's CPU time (`clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID)`; the engine is
`thread_local!`, so the render runs on that thread) under `BUDGET_MS`. It is still a real
check. The claim is what the path costs to measure, and CPU time counts exactly that work
while leaving out the time a busy host kept the thread off a core. On an idle host the two
agree. At a load average of 94, R2 took 17.3 ms of CPU (17.8 wall) and R4 68.4 ms (68.5
wall). A regression that made the memo re-measure, or made the measuring slower, still
fails it at the same 250 ms.

**Verification.**
- `make typecheck`: 0 errors, exactly the four baseline warnings. The probe typecheck: ok.
- `encoder_limit_proof.py --probe`: 13/13. Mutants `tip-drops-hold`, `estimate-no-count`
  and `row-says-waiting` (Q4 widened): each CAUGHT, failing only the row it names. The
  other nine mutants' anchors and rows were untouched and were not re-run: **12 mutants,
  12 caught**.
- `cd graphic && cargo test --release --test path`: 6/6 at a load average of 94.
- `spec_index_proof.py`: 210/210 (§7.8 614 → 616, `codec-export.md` 572 → 573, the folder
  14323 → 14324).
- `phase7_chrome.py`: **79/79** (was 75/79). The opaque control's winner was 0 pt with 0
  rows, runner-up 74; the translucent note was 22 pt with 0 of 270 rows, runner-up 100; the
  note's ink was the accent (52, 120, 246); 0.99 → 22 pt, 0.999 → 0 pt.
- `make gate`: PASS (test 171 s, app 187 s), at a load of about 70–95 from the C5 lane.
- `RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/encoder_limit_proof.py`: 17/17.
  `RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/export_status_proof.py`: 9/9. No instance log
  carried a `Frame Job: ` line.
